meeting_header: Date: 2026-04-05T14:30:00-07:00\nDuration: 52 minutes\nAttendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Neill (Redwood SE), Rita Alvarez (Paladin CTO), Samir Patel (Paladin SRE), Noah Kim (Paladin PM)
summary: POC scoping focused on integration planning: confirm success criteria (latency P95, throughput), workload sizing, benchmark plan, timeline (2-4 week pilot), and technical approach for SDKs and OpenAI-compatible endpoints including function/tool calling and structured JSON outputs. Security and data residency questions noted; Redwood to send SOC2, KMS details and SDK examples.
topics: Integration: SDKs, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling
Security: SOC2, KMS, RBAC, data retention
transcript:
00:00 Maya: okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll kick off, I'm Maya from Redwood, that's Liam from our SE team - quick intros?
00:08 Rita: hi, Rita, CTO at Paladin Security, Samir's my SRE lead and Noah on product
00:15 Samir: hey
00:16 Liam: great thanks, um the goal today is to scope the POC, figure success criteria, bench plan, and the integration path, especially around your OpenAI-compat usage and function calling needs
00:30 Noah: yea we have two main use cases: automated incident summarization and a threat-scoring enrichment pipeline that calls third-party tools. We want structured JSON outputs for both
00:45 Maya: perfect, can you share current traffic and latency targets?
00:50 Rita: production for the summarization is roughly 200 requests per minute during peak, avg payload around 800 tokens, sometimes bursts to 500 rpm but most steady at 200 rpm. For enrichment we do about 50 concurrent calls, each call needs sub-second-ish response ideally, but we can accept up to 300ms p95? um 300 to 400ms?
01:20 Liam: ok so two distinct workloads; for the summarization CPU-bound token generation and for enrichment we have low latency requirements and tool-calling. For success criteria, do you want P95 under 400ms for enrichment and cost under $X per million tokens?
01:35 Noah: cost is important but first we need functional correctness: JSON schema must be exact for downstream ingestion, no fuzziness. If output schema fails, it breaks our pipeline.
01:50 Maya: noted, we'll plan a schema validation test as part of benchmarks. We'll show examples in the SDK.
02:05 Rita: also the compliance bar: SOC2 is minimum, plus we need KMS integration and audit logs, SSO for the Redwood console, and data not to leave region EU if possible
02:20 Liam: Redwood Private can do VPC and on-prem options, and our Dedicated offering supports customer KMS via AWS KMS or HSMs. We'll send the SOC2 and the KMS integration docs.
02:35 Maya: technical question - are you planning to call Redwood via our OpenAI-compatible endpoints or via native SDKs?
02:42 Noah: we prefer OpenAI-compat so we don't change existing code, but we might use the SDK for function-calling helpers
02:50 Liam: good, our endpoints support the OpenAI completions/chat/embeddings surface. Function/tool calling is supported; note that function calling payload constraints differ a bit depending on model/quantization - also small transcription note: sometimes the product name is Redwood Dedicateed in our docs, but it's Dedicated
03:12 Rita: ha, alright. For the POC timeline what do you recommend?
03:18 Maya: typical is 2-4 weeks: week 1 ingest sample corpus and size; week 2 run baseline benchmarks (latency p50/p95, tokens/sec), week 3 iterate on config (batching, kv cache, quantization), week 4 acceptance and handoff. For you with compliance checks, maybe push to 4 weeks
03:40 Samir: for workload sizing we can give a 7-day trace of requests and a few sample payloads - will that work?
03:48 Maya: perfect. For benchmarks we'll test both Hosted and Dedicated variants; we'll run throughput tests with increasing concurrency to find optimal batching and compute profile. We'll measure p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost estimates
04:05 Noah: what about structured output validation? We need to assert the JSON matches schema for 1,000 samples with zero schema failures as part of acceptance
04:15 Liam: fair, we'll add a schema conformance test in the benchmark harness; we'll also add a small RLHF/temperature sweep to test robustness for edge cases
04:28 Rita: encryption - how do we handle logs and KV cache? retention?
04:32 Liam: logs are optional; we can disable logging of request bodies and only store metadata. KV cache is ephemeral in the runtime; for private deployments you control persistence. Retention policies we can set per-customer
04:45 Maya: ok recap success criteria: 1) enrichment P95 <= 400ms (or agreed number) 2) summarization throughput meets 200 rpm with p95 latency under 1.2s 3) JSON schema conformance 4) Security checklist met (SOC2, KMS, SSO)
05:05 Samir: question on function calling - we call external tool endpoints as part of the chain, do you support tool chaining natively?
05:12 Liam: yes you can do function/tool calling, the runtime supports tool invocation hooks; for POC we'll provide a sample adapter that proxies tool calls to your internal services. There's some nuance around streaming and partial outputs - we'll provide examples in the SDK
05:30 Noah: any known limitations with OpenAI-compat? e.g., model names or certain fields missing
05:36 Liam: most common is differences in response envelope and some lower-level metadata fields; function_call semantics are largely compatible but path names can differ. We'll share an OpenAI-compat shim and code snippets for both Node and Python
05:50 Rita: timeline for docs & SDK?
05:53 Maya: I'll send SOC2 + security pack by 4/7, Liam will post SDK examples by 4/8, and we'll schedule a benchmark window for 4/12-4/16. Paladin to send sample traffic by 4/9
06:05 Noah: agreed
06:08 Rita: one more thing - can you do regional restriction to EU? Data residency is critical
06:12 Liam: yes we have EU regions and Private deployments can be strictly regional; for Hosted we'll route to EU region endpoints. We'll include region config in the guide
06:25 Samir: regarding throughput, for summarization can Redwood handle bursts to 500 rpm without cold starts?
06:31 Liam: we'll test burst behavior in the benchmark; Dedicated with reserved capacity handles bursts better. We'll also show autoscaling settings and burst pools
06:45 Maya: any blockers on your side?
06:48 Rita: just legal review time - procurement may need a separate session. Also we'll validate security docs
06:55 Maya: okay we'll loop in our partnerships team if procurement gets involved.
07:02 Noah: do you have a sample OpenAPI schema for the JSON output?
07:06 Liam: yes we'll include an example JSON schema and the SDK will include a validator helper. We'll include unit tests for 1k samples as part of the harness
07:18 Rita: great. quick note, sometimes transcriptions say 'KV cache' as 'K V cash' in alarms, so don't mind slight typos in this transcript
07:26 Maya: haha noted. any final Qs?
07:28 Samir: none from me
07:29 Noah: all good
07:30 Maya: thanks everyone, next steps as discussed, we'll send a calendar invite for the benchmark window and internal follow-ups
07:37 Meeting end
